Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) \) be a nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solution defined on \( M \times  \left( {-\infty , T}\right) \) (for some \( T > 0 \) ), where \( M \) is a two-dimensional manifold. Note that the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution satisfies the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality (Corollary 2.5.5). In particular by Corollary 2.5.8, the scalar curvature of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is pointwise nondecreasing in time. Moreover by the strong maximum principle, the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution has strictly positive curvature everywhere.

By the above Theorem 6.2.1, we know that the scalings of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution along a sequence of points \( {q}_{k} \) in \( M \) and a sequence of times \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow   - \infty \) converge to a nonflat gradient shrinking soliton \( \left( {\bar{M},{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) with \( - \infty  < t \leq  0 \) .

We first show that the limiting gradient shrinking soliton \( \left( {\bar{M},{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) has uniformly bounded curvature. Clearly, the limiting soliton has nonnegative curvature and is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales, and its scalar curvature is still pointwise nondecreasing in time. Thus we only need to show that the limiting soliton has bounded curvature at \( t = 0 \) . We argue by contradiction. Suppose the curvature of the limiting soliton is unbounded at \( t = 0 \) . Of course in this case the limiting soliton \( \bar{M} \) is noncompact. Then by applying Lemma 6.1.4, we can choose a sequence of points \( {x}_{j}, j = 1,2,\ldots \) , divergent to infinity such that the scalar curvature \( \bar{R} \) of the limit satisfies

\[
\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  \geq  j\text{ and }\bar{R}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  4\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)
\]

for all \( j = 1,2,\ldots \) , and \( x \in  {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{j}, j/\sqrt{R\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) }}\right) \) . And then by the nondecreasing (in time) of the scalar curvature, we have

\[
\bar{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  4\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) ,
\]

for all \( j = 1,2,\ldots , x \in  {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{j}, j/\sqrt{R\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) }}\right) \) and \( t \leq  0 \) . By combining with Hamilton’s compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5) and the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing, we know that a subsequence of the rescaling solutions

\[
\left( {\bar{M},\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) {\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x, t/\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) }\right) ,{x}_{j}}\right) ,\;j = 1,2,\ldots ,
\]

converges in the \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) topology to a nonflat smooth solution of the Ricci flow. Then Proposition 6.1.2 implies that the new (two-dimensional) limit must be flat. This arrives at a contradiction. So we have proved that the limiting gradient shrinking soliton has uniformly bounded curvature.

We next show that the limiting soliton is compact. Suppose the limiting soliton is (complete and) noncompact. By the strong maximum principle we know that the limiting soliton also has strictly positive curvature everywhere. After a shift of the time, we may assume that the limiting soliton satisfies the following equation

(6.2.24)

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f + {\bar{R}}_{ij} + \frac{1}{2t}{\bar{g}}_{ij} = 0,\;\text{ on } - \infty  < t < 0,
\]

everywhere for some function \( f \) . Differentiating the equation (6.2.24) and switching the order of differentiations, as in the derivation of (1.1.14), we get

(6.2.25)

\[
{\nabla }_{i}\bar{R} = 2{\bar{R}}_{ij}{\nabla }_{j}f.
\]

Fix some \( t < 0 \) , say \( t =  - 1 \) , and consider a long shortest geodesic \( \gamma \left( s\right) ,0 \leq  s \leq  \bar{s} \) . Let \( {x}_{0} = \gamma \left( 0\right) \) and \( X\left( s\right)  = \dot{\gamma }\left( s\right) \) . Let \( V\left( 0\right) \) be any unit vector orthogonal to \( \dot{\gamma }\left( 0\right) \) and translate \( V\left( 0\right) \) along \( \gamma \left( s\right) \) to get a parallel vector field \( V\left( s\right) ,0 \leq  s \leq  \bar{s} \) on \( \gamma \) . Set

\[
\widehat{V}\left( s\right)  = \left\{  \begin{array}{ll} {sV}\left( s\right) , & \text{ for }0 \leq  s \leq  1, \\  V\left( s\right) , & \text{ for }1 \leq  s \leq  \bar{s} - 1, \\  \left( {\bar{s} - s}\right) V\left( s\right) , & \text{ for }\bar{s} - 1 \leq  s \leq  \bar{s}. \end{array}\right.
\]

It follows from the second variation formula of arclength that

\[
{\int }_{0}^{\bar{s}}\left( {{\left| \dot{\widehat{V}}\left( s\right) \right| }^{2} - \bar{R}\left( {X,\widehat{V}, X,\widehat{V}}\right) }\right) {ds} \geq  0.
\]

Thus we clearly have

\[
{\int }_{0}^{\bar{s}}\bar{R}\left( {X,\widehat{V}, X,\widehat{V}}\right) {ds} \leq  \text{ const., }
\]

and then

(6.2.26)

\[
{\int }_{0}^{\bar{s}}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds} \leq  \text{ const.. }
\]

By integrating the equation (6.2.24) we get

\[
X\left( {f\left( {\gamma \left( \bar{s}\right) }\right) }\right)  - X\left( {f\left( {\gamma \left( 0\right) }\right) }\right)  + {\int }_{0}^{\bar{s}}\operatorname{Ric}\left( {X, X}\right) {ds} - \frac{1}{2}\bar{s} = 0
\]

and then by (6.2.26), we deduce

\[
\frac{d}{ds}\left( {f \circ  \gamma \left( s\right) }\right)  \geq  \frac{s}{2} - \text{ const. },
\]

\[
\text{ and }f \circ  \gamma \left( s\right)  \geq  \frac{{s}^{2}}{4} - \text{ const. } \cdot  s - \text{ const. }
\]

for \( s > 0 \) large enough. Thus at large distances from the fixed point \( {x}_{0} \) the function \( f \) has no critical points and is proper. It then follows from the Morse theory that any two high level sets of \( f \) are diffeomorphic via the gradient curves of \( f \) . Since by (6.2.25),

\[
\frac{d}{ds}\bar{R}\left( {\eta \left( s\right) , - 1}\right)  = \langle \nabla \bar{R},\dot{\eta }\left( s\right) \rangle
\]

\[
= 2{\bar{R}}_{ij}{\nabla }_{i}f{\nabla }_{j}f
\]

\[
\geq  0
\]

for any integral curve \( \eta \left( s\right) \) of \( \nabla f \) , we conclude that the scalar curvature \( \bar{R}\left( {x, - 1}\right) \) has a positive lower bound on \( \bar{M} \) , which contradicts the Bonnet-Myers Theorem. So we have proved that the limiting gradient shrinking soliton is compact.

By Proposition 5.1.10, the compact limiting gradient shrinking soliton has constant curvature. This says that the scalings of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) along a sequence of points \( {q}_{k} \in  M \) and a sequence of times \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow   - \infty \) converge in the \( {C}^{\infty } \) topology to the round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) or the round \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{2} \) . In particular, by looking at the time derivative of the volume and the Gauss-Bonnet theorem, we know that the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) exists on a maximal time interval \( \left( {-\infty , T}\right) \) with \( T <  + \infty \) .

Consider the scaled entropy of Hamilton [60]

\[
E\left( t\right)  = {\int }_{M}R\log \left\lbrack  {R\left( {T - t}\right) }\right\rbrack  d{V}_{t}
\]

We compute

(6.2.27)

\[
\frac{d}{dt}E\left( t\right)  = {\int }_{M}\log \left\lbrack  {R\left( {T - t}\right) }\right\rbrack  {\Delta Rd}{V}_{t} + {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {{\Delta R} + {R}^{2} - \frac{R}{\left( T - t\right) }}\right\rbrack  d{V}_{t}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {-\frac{{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}}{R} + {R}^{2} - {rR}}\right\rbrack  d{V}_{t}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{M}\left\lbrack  {-\frac{{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}}{R} + {\left( R - r\right) }^{2}}\right\rbrack  d{V}_{t}
\]

where \( r = {\int }_{M}{Rd}{V}_{t}/{\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( M\right) \) and we have used \( {\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( M\right)  = \left( {{\int }_{M}{Rd}{V}_{t}}\right)  \cdot  \left( {T - t}\right) \) (by the Gauss-Bonnet theorem).

For a smooth function \( f \) on the surface \( M \) , one can readily check

\[
{\int }_{M}{\left( \Delta f\right) }^{2} = 2{\int }_{M}{\left| {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2}\left( \Delta f\right) {g}_{ij}\right| }^{2} + {\int }_{M}R{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2},
\]

\[
{\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R + R\nabla f\right| }^{2}}{R} = {\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}}{R} - 2{\int }_{M}R\left( {\Delta f}\right)  + {\int }_{M}R{\left| \nabla f\right| }^{2},
\]

and then

\[
{\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}}{R} + {\int }_{M}\left( {\Delta f}\right) \left( {{\Delta f} - {2R}}\right)
\]

\[
= 2{\int }_{M}{\left| {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2}\left( \Delta f\right) {g}_{ij}\right| }^{2} + {\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R + R\nabla f\right| }^{2}}{R}.
\]

By choosing \( {\Delta f} = R - r \) , we get

\[
{\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}}{R} - {\int }_{M}{\left( R - r\right) }^{2}
\]

\[
= 2{\int }_{M}{\left| {\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2}\left( \Delta f\right) {g}_{ij}\right| }^{2} + {\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R + R\nabla f\right| }^{2}}{R} \geq  0.
\]

If the equality holds, then we have

\[
{\nabla }_{i}{\nabla }_{j}f - \frac{1}{2}\left( {\Delta f}\right) {g}_{ij} = 0
\]

i.e., \( \nabla f \) is conformal. By the Kazdan-Warner identity [77], it follows that

\[
{\int }_{M}\nabla R \cdot  \nabla f = 0
\]

so

\[
0 =  - {\int }_{M}{R\Delta f}
\]

\[
=  - {\int }_{M}{\left( R - r\right) }^{2}.
\]

Hence we have proved the following inequality due to Chow [37]

(6.2.28)

\[
{\int }_{M}\frac{{\left| \nabla R\right| }^{2}}{R} \geq  {\int }_{M}{\left( R - r\right) }^{2}
\]

and the equality holds if and only if \( R \equiv  r \) .

The combination (6.2.27) and (6.2.28) shows that the scaled entropy \( E\left( t\right) \) is strictly decreasing along the Ricci flow unless we are on the round sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) or its quotient \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{2} \) . Moreover the convergence result in Theorem 5.1.11 shows that the scaled entropy \( E \) has its minimum value at the constant curvature metric (round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) or round \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{2} \) ). We had shown that the scalings of the nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solution along a sequence of times \( {t}_{k} \rightarrow   - \infty \) converge to the constant curvature metric. Then \( E\left( t\right) \) has its minimal value at \( t =  - \infty \) , so it was constant all along, hence the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution must have constant curvature for each \( t \in  \left( {-\infty , T}\right) \) . This proves the theorem.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
(Canonical neighborhood theorem). For any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) one can find positive constants \( {C}_{1} = {C}_{1}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) and \( {C}_{2} = {C}_{2}\left( \varepsilon \right) \) with the following property. Suppose we have a three-dimensional nonflat (compact or noncompact) ancient \( \kappa \) - solution \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) . Then either the ancient solution is the round \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) , or every point \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) has an open neighborhood \( B \) , with \( {B}_{t}\left( {x, r}\right)  \subset  B \subset  {B}_{t}\left( {x,{2r}}\right) \) for some \( 0 < r < {C}_{1}R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , which falls into one of the following three categories:

(a) \( B \) is an evolving \( \varepsilon \) -neck (in the sense that it is the slice at the time \( t \) of the parabolic region \( \left\{  {\left( {{x}^{\prime },{t}^{\prime }}\right)  \mid  {x}^{\prime } \in  B,{t}^{\prime } \in  \left\lbrack  {t - {\varepsilon }^{-2}R{\left( x, t\right) }^{-1}, t}\right\rbrack  }\right\} \) which is, after scaling with factor \( R\left( {x, t}\right) \) and shifting the time \( t \) to zero, \( \varepsilon \) -close (in the \( {C}^{\left\lbrack  {\varepsilon }^{-1}\right\rbrack  } \) topology) to the subset \( \left( {{\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{I}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {-{\varepsilon }^{-2},0}\right\rbrack \) of the evolving standard round cylinder with scalar curvature 1 and length \( 2{\varepsilon }^{-1} \) to \( \mathbb{I} \) at the time zero), or

(b) \( B \) is an evolving \( \varepsilon \) -cap (in the sense that it is the time slice at the time \( t \) of an evolving metric on \( {\mathbb{B}}^{3} \) or \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{3} \smallsetminus  {\mathbb{B}}^{3} \) such that the region outside some suitable compact subset of \( {\mathbb{B}}^{3} \) or \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{3} \smallsetminus  {\mathbb{B}}^{3} \) is an evolving \( \varepsilon \) -neck), or

(c) \( B \) is a compact manifold (without boundary) with positive sectional curvature (thus it is diffeomorphic to the round three-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) or a metric quotient of \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3}) \)

furthermore, the scalar curvature of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution on \( B \) at time \( t \) is between \( {C}_{2}^{-1}R\left( {x, t}\right) \) and \( {C}_{2}R\left( {x, t}\right) \) , and the volume of \( B \) in case (a) and case (b) satisfies

\[
{\left( {C}_{2}R\left( x, t\right) \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}} \leq  {\operatorname{Vol}}_{t}\left( B\right)  \leq  \varepsilon {r}^{3}.
\]

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
As before, we first consider the easy case that the curvature operator has a nontrivial null vector somewhere at some time. By pulling back the solution to its universal cover and applying Hamilton's strong maximum principle and Theorem 6.2.2, we deduce that the universal cover is the evolving round cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Then exactly as before, by the argument in the proof of Lemma 6.4.1, we conclude that the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is isometric to the round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R},{\mathbb{{RP}}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) , or the twisted product \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2}\widetilde{ \times  }\mathbb{R} \) where \( {\mathbb{Z}}_{2} \) flips both \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) and \( \mathbb{R} \) . Clearly each point of the round cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) or the twisted product \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2}\widetilde{ \times  }\mathbb{R} \) has a neighborhood falling into the category (a) or (b) (over \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{3} \smallsetminus  \overline{{\mathbb{B}}^{3}} \) ).

We now assume that the curvature operator of the nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is positive everywhere. Then the manifold is orientable by the Cheeger-Gromoll theorem [23] for the noncompact case or the Synge theorem [22] for the compact case.

Without loss of generality, we may assume \( \varepsilon \) is suitably small, say \( 0 < \varepsilon  < \frac{1}{100} \) . If the nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is noncompact, the conclusions follow immediately from the combination of Corollary 6.4.5 and Theorem 6.4.3(i). Thus we may assume the nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is compact. By Proposition 6.4.2, either the compact ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is isometric to a metric quotient of the round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) , or it is \( {\kappa }_{{0}^{ - }} \) noncollapsed on all scales for the universal positive constant \( {\kappa }_{0} \) . Clearly each point of a metric quotient of the round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) has a neighborhood falling into category (c). Thus we may further assume the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is also \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -noncollapsing.

We argue by contradiction. Suppose that for some \( \varepsilon  \in  \left( {0,\frac{1}{100}}\right) \) , there exist a sequence of compact orientable ancient \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -solutions \( \left( {{M}_{k},{g}_{k}}\right) \) with positive curvature operator, a sequence of points \( \left( {{x}_{k},0}\right) \) with \( {x}_{k} \in  {M}_{k} \) and sequences of positive constants \( {C}_{1k} \rightarrow  \infty \) and \( {C}_{2k} = \omega \left( {4{C}_{1k}^{2}}\right) \) , with the function \( \omega \) given in Theorem 6.4.3, such that for every radius \( r,0 < r < {C}_{1k}R{\left( {x}_{k},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) , any open neighborhood \( B \) , with \( {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{k}, r}\right)  \subset  B \subset  {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{k},{2r}}\right) \) , does not fall into one of the three categories (a),(b) and (c), where in the case (a) and case (b), we require the neighborhood \( B \) to satisfy the volume estimate

\[
{\left( {C}_{2k}R\left( {x}_{k},0\right) \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}} \leq  {\operatorname{Vol}}_{0}\left( B\right)  \leq  \varepsilon {r}^{3}.
\]

By Theorem 6.4.3(i) and the choice of the constants \( {C}_{2k} \) we see that the diameter of each \( {M}_{k} \) at \( t = 0 \) is at least \( {C}_{1k}R{\left( {x}_{k},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) ; otherwise we can choose suitable \( r \in  \left( {0,{C}_{1k}R{\left( {x}_{k},0\right) }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right) \) and \( B = {M}_{k} \) , which falls into the category (c) with the scalar curvature between \( {C}_{2k}^{-1}R\left( {x,0}\right) \) and \( {C}_{2k}R\left( {x,0}\right) \) on \( B \) . Now by scaling the ancient \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -solutions along the points \( \left( {{x}_{k},0}\right) \) with factors \( R\left( {{x}_{k},0}\right) \) , it follows from Corollary 6.4.4 that a sequence of the ancient \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -solutions converge in the \( {C}_{loc}^{\infty } \) topology to a noncompact orientable ancient \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -solution.

If the curvature operator of the noncompact limit has a nontrivial null vector somewhere at some time, it follows exactly as before by using the argument in the proof of Lemma 6.4.1 that the orientable limit is isometric to the round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) , or the twisted product \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) where \( {\mathbb{Z}}_{2} \) flips both \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \) and \( \mathbb{R} \) . Then for \( k \) large enough, a suitable neighborhood \( B \) (for suitable \( r \) ) of the point \( \left( {{x}_{k},0}\right) \) would fall into the category (a) or (b) (over \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{3} \smallsetminus  {\mathbb{B}}^{3} \) ) with the desired volume estimate. This is a contradiction.

If the noncompact limit has positive sectional curvature everywhere, then by using Corollary 6.4.5 and Theorem 6.4.3(i) for the noncompact limit we see that for \( k \) large enough, a suitable neighborhood \( B \) (for suitable \( r \) ) of the point \( \left( {{x}_{k},0}\right) \) would fall into category (a) or (b) (over \( {\mathbb{B}}^{3} \) ) with the desired volume estimate. This is also a contradiction.

Finally, the statement on the curvature estimate in the neighborhood \( B \) follows directly from Theorem 6.4.3(i). 0

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
Let \( {g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) , x \in  M \) and \( t \in  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) , be a nonflat ancient \( \kappa \) -solution for some \( \kappa  > 0 \) . For an arbitrary point \( \left( {p,{t}_{0}}\right)  \in  M \times  ( - \infty ,0\rbrack \) , we define as in Chapter 3 that

\[
\tau  = {t}_{0} - t,\;\text{ for }t < {t}_{0},
\]

\[
l\left( {q,\tau }\right)  = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{\tau }}\inf \left\{  {{\int }_{0}^{\tau }\sqrt{s}\left( {R\left( {\gamma \left( s\right) ,{t}_{0} - s}\right)  + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( s\right) \right| }_{{g}_{ij}\left( {{t}_{0} - s}\right) }^{2}}\right) {ds} \mid  }\right.
\]

\[
\gamma  : \left\lbrack  {0,\tau }\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M\text{ with }\left. {\gamma \left( 0\right)  = p,\gamma \left( \tau \right)  = q}\right\}  ,
\]

\[
\text{ and }\widetilde{V}\left( \tau \right)  = {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\tau }\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{0} - \tau }\left( q\right) \text{ . }
\]

Recall from (6.2.1) that for each \( \tau  > 0 \) we can find \( q = q\left( \tau \right) \) such that \( l\left( {q,\tau }\right)  \leq  \frac{3}{2} \) . In view of Lemma 6.4.1, we may assume that the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is not a gradient shrinking Ricci soliton. Thus by (the proof of) Theorem 6.2.1, the scalings of \( {g}_{ij}\left( {{t}_{0} - \tau }\right) \) at \( q\left( \tau \right) \) with factor \( {\tau }^{-1} \) converge along a subsequence of \( \tau  \rightarrow   + \infty \) to a nonflat gradient shrinking soliton with nonnegative curvature operator which is \( \kappa \) -noncollapsed on all scales. We now show that the limit has bounded curvature.

Denote the limiting nonflat gradient shrinking soliton by \( \left( {\bar{M},{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) with \( - \infty  < \; t \leq  0 \) . Note that there holds the Li-Yau-Hamilton inequality (Theorem 2.5.4) on any ancient \( \kappa \) -solution and in particular, the scalar curvature of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is pointwise nondecreasing in time. This implies that the scalar curvature of the limiting soliton \( \left( {\bar{M},{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) is still pointwise nondecreasing in time. Thus we only need to show that the limiting soliton has bounded curvature at \( t = 0 \) .

We argue by contradiction. By lifting to its orientable cover, we may assume that \( \bar{M} \) is orientable. Suppose the curvature of the limiting soliton is unbounded at \( t = 0 \) . Of course in this case the limiting soliton \( \bar{M} \) is noncompact. Then by applying Lemma 6.1.4, we can choose a sequence of points \( {x}_{j}, j = 1,2,\ldots \) , divergent to infinity such that the scalar curvature \( \bar{R} \) of the limit satisfies

\[
\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  \geq  j\text{ and }\bar{R}\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  4\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{j}, j/\sqrt{\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) }}\right) \) and \( j = 1,2,\ldots \) Since the scalar curvature is nondecreasing in time, we have

(6.4.10)

\[
\bar{R}\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  4\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) ,
\]

for all \( x \in  {B}_{0}\left( {{x}_{j}, j/\sqrt{\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) }}\right) \) , all \( t \leq  0 \) and \( j = 1,2,\ldots \) By combining with Hamilton’s compactness theorem (Theorem 4.1.5) and the \( \kappa \) -noncollapsing, we know that a subsequence of the rescaled solutions

\[
\left( {\bar{M},\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) {\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x, t/\bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right) }\right) ,{x}_{j}}\right) ,\;j = 1,2,\ldots ,
\]

converges in the \( {C}_{\text{ loc }}^{\infty } \) topology to a nonflat smooth solution of the Ricci flow. Then Proposition 6.1.2 implies that the new limit at the new time \( \{ t = 0\} \) must split off a line. By pulling back the new limit to its universal cover and applying Hamilton's strong maximum principle, we deduce that the pull-back of the new limit on the universal cover splits off a line for all time \( t \leq  0 \) . Thus by combining with Theorem 6.2.2 and the argument in the proof of Lemma 6.4.1, we further deduce that the new limit is either the round cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) or the round \( {\mathbb{{RP}}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Since \( \bar{M} \) is orientable, the new limit must be \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) . Since \( \left( {\bar{M},{\bar{g}}_{ij}\left( {x,0}\right) }\right) \) has nonnegative curvature operator and the points \( \left\{  {x}_{j}\right\} \) going to infinity and \( \bar{R}\left( {{x}_{j},0}\right)  \rightarrow   + \infty \) , this gives a contradiction to Proposition 6.1.1. So we have proved that the limiting gradient shrinking soliton has bounded curvature at each time.

Hence by Lemma 6.4.1, the limiting gradient shrinking soliton is either the round three-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) or its metric quotients, or the infinite cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) or one of its \( {\mathbb{Z}}_{2} \) quotients. If the asymptotic gradient shrinking soliton is the round three-sphere \( {\mathbb{S}}^{3} \) or its metric quotients, it follows from Lemma 5.2.4 and Proposition 5.2.5 that the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution must be round. Thus in the following we may assume the asymptotic gradient shrinking soliton is the infinite cylinder \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) or a \( {\mathbb{Z}}_{2} \) quotient of \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) .

We now come back to consider the original ancient \( \kappa \) -solution \( \left( {M,{g}_{ij}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) \) . By rescaling, we can assume that \( R\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  1 \) for all \( \left( {x, t}\right) \) satisfying \( {d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {x, p}\right)  \leq  2 \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - 1,{t}_{0}}\right\rbrack \) . We will argue as in the proof of Theorem 3.3.2 (Perelman’s no local collapsing theorem I) to obtain a positive lower bound for \( {\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,1}\right) }\right) \) .

Denote by \( \xi  = {\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}{\left( {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( p,1\right) \right) }^{\frac{1}{3}} \) . For any \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) we can find an \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic \( \gamma \left( \tau \right) \) , starting at \( p \) , with \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right)  = v \) . It follows from the \( \mathcal{L} \) -geodesic equation (3.2.1) that

\[
\frac{d}{d\tau }\left( {\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }}\right)  - \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{\tau }\nabla R + 2\operatorname{Ric}\left( {\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }, \cdot  }\right)  = 0.
\]

By integrating as before we see that for \( \tau  \leq  \xi \) with the property \( \gamma \left( \sigma \right)  \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,1}\right) \) as long as \( \sigma  < \tau \) , there holds

\[
\left| {\sqrt{\tau }\dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right)  - v}\right|  \leq  {C\xi }\left( {\left| v\right|  + 1}\right)
\]

where \( C \) is some positive constant depending only on the dimension. Without loss of generality, we may assume \( {C\xi } \leq  \frac{1}{4} \) and \( \xi  \leq  \frac{1}{100} \) . Then for \( v \in  {T}_{p}M \) with \( \left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}} \) and for \( \tau  \leq  \xi \) with the property \( \gamma \left( \sigma \right)  \in  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,1}\right) \) as long as \( \sigma  < \tau \) , we have

\[
{d}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,\gamma \left( \tau \right) }\right)  \leq  {\int }_{0}^{\tau }\left| {\dot{\gamma }\left( \sigma \right) }\right| {d\sigma }
\]

\[
< \frac{1}{2}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}{\int }_{0}^{\tau }\frac{d\sigma }{\sqrt{\sigma }}
\]

\[
= 1\text{ . }
\]

This shows

(6.4.11)

\[
\mathcal{L}\exp \left\{  {\left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\}  \left( \xi \right)  \subset  {B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,1}\right) .
\]

We decompose Perelman’s reduced volume \( \widetilde{V}\left( \xi \right) \) as

(6.4.12)

\[
\widetilde{V}\left( \xi \right)  = {\int }_{\mathcal{L}\exp \left\{  {\left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\}  \left( \xi \right) }
\]

\[
+ {\int }_{M \smallsetminus  \mathcal{L}\exp \left\{  {\left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\}  \left( \xi \right) }{\left( 4\pi \xi \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\xi }\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{0} - \xi }\left( q\right) .
\]

By using (6.4.11) and the metric evolution equation of the Ricci flow, the first term on the RHS of (6.4.12) can be estimated by

\[
{\int }_{\mathcal{L}\exp \left\{  {\left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\}  \left( \xi \right) }{\left( 4\pi \xi \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\xi }\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{0} - \xi }\left( q\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,1}\right) }{\left( 4\pi \xi \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}{e}^{3\xi }d{V}_{{t}_{0}}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
= {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}{e}^{3\xi }{\xi }^{\frac{3}{2}}
\]

\[
< {\xi }^{\frac{3}{2}}\text{ , }
\]

while by using Theorem 3.2.7 (Perelman's Jacobian comparison theorem), the second term on the RHS of (6.4.12) can be estimated by

(6.4.13)

\[
{\int }_{M \smallsetminus  \mathcal{L}\exp \left\{  {\left| v\right|  \leq  \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}}\right\}  \left( \xi \right) }{\left( 4\pi \xi \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,\xi }\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{0} - \xi }\left( q\right)
\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{\left\{  \left| v\right|  > \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right\}  }{\left( 4\pi \tau \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}{\left. \exp \left( -l\left( \tau \right) \right) \mathcal{J}\left( \tau \right) \right| }_{\tau  = 0}{dv}
\]

\[
= {\left( 4\pi \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}{\int }_{\left\{  \left| v\right|  > \frac{1}{4}{\xi }^{-\frac{1}{2}}\right\}  }\exp \left( {-{\left| v\right| }^{2}}\right) {dv}
\]

\[
< {\xi }^{\frac{3}{2}}
\]

since \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}{\tau }^{-\frac{3}{2}}\mathcal{J}\left( \tau \right)  = 1 \) and \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{\tau  \rightarrow  {0}^{ + }}}l\left( \tau \right)  = {\left| v\right| }^{2} \) by (3.2.18) and (3.2.19) respectively. Thus we obtain

(6.4.14)

\[
\widetilde{V}\left( \xi \right)  < 2{\xi }^{\frac{3}{2}}.
\]

On the other hand, we recall that there exist a sequence \( {\tau }_{k} \rightarrow   + \infty \) and a sequence of points \( q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right)  \in  M \) with \( l\left( {q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) ,{\tau }_{k}}\right)  \leq  \frac{3}{2} \) so that the scalings of the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution at \( q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) \) with factor \( {\tau }_{k}^{-1} \) converge to either round \( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) or one of its \( {\mathbb{Z}}_{2} \) quotients. For sufficiently large \( k \) , we construct a path \( \gamma  : \;\left\lbrack  {0,2{\tau }_{k}}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  M \) , connecting \( p \) to any given point \( q \in  M \) , as follows: the first half path \( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  0,{\tau }_{k}\right\rbrack  } \) connects \( p \) to \( q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) \) such that

\[
l\left( {q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) ,{\tau }_{k}}\right)  = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{{\tau }_{k}}}{\int }_{0}^{{\tau }_{k}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {R + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau } \leq  2,
\]

and the second half path \( {\left. \gamma \right| }_{\left\lbrack  {\tau }_{k},2{\tau }_{k}\right\rbrack  } \) is a shortest geodesic connecting \( q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) \) to \( q \) with respect to the metric \( {g}_{ij}\left( {{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{k}}\right) \) . Note that the rescaled metric \( {\tau }_{k}^{-1}{g}_{ij}\left( {{t}_{0} - \tau }\right) \) over the domain \( {B}_{{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{k}}\left( {q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) ,\sqrt{{\tau }_{k}}}\right)  \times  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0} - 2{\tau }_{k},{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{k}}\right\rbrack \) is sufficiently close to the round

\( {\mathbb{S}}^{2} \times  \mathbb{R} \) or its \( {\mathbb{Z}}_{2} \) quotients. Then there is a universal positive constant \( \beta \) such that

\[
l\left( {q,2{\tau }_{k}}\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2{\tau }_{k}}}\left( {{\int }_{0}^{{\tau }_{k}} + {\int }_{{\tau }_{k}}^{2{\tau }_{k}}}\right) \sqrt{\tau }\left( {R + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
\leq  \sqrt{2} + \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2{\tau }_{k}}}{\int }_{{\tau }_{k}}^{2{\tau }_{k}}\sqrt{\tau }\left( {R + {\left| \dot{\gamma }\left( \tau \right) \right| }^{2}}\right) {d\tau }
\]

\[
\leq  \beta
\]

for all \( q \in  {B}_{{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{k}}\left( {q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) ,\sqrt{{\tau }_{k}}}\right) \) . Thus

\[
\widetilde{V}\left( {2{\tau }_{k}}\right)  = {\int }_{M}{\left( 4\pi \left( 2{\tau }_{k}\right) \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}\exp \left( {-l\left( {q,2{\tau }_{k}}\right) }\right) d{V}_{{t}_{0} - 2{\tau }_{k}}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
\geq  {e}^{-\beta }{\int }_{{B}_{{t}_{0} - {\tau }_{k}}\left( {q\left( {\tau }_{k}\right) ,\sqrt{{\tau }_{k}}}\right) }{\left( 4\pi \left( 2{\tau }_{k}\right) \right) }^{-\frac{3}{2}}d{V}_{{t}_{0} - 2{\tau }_{k}}\left( q\right)
\]

\[
\geq  \widetilde{\beta }
\]

for some universal positive constant \( \widetilde{\beta } \) . Here we have used the curvature estimate (6.2.6). By combining with the monotonicity of Perelman's reduced volume (Theorem 3.2.8) and (6.4.14), we deduce that

\[
\widetilde{\beta } \leq  \widetilde{V}\left( {2{\tau }_{k}}\right)  \leq  \widetilde{V}\left( \xi \right)  < 2{\xi }^{\frac{3}{2}}.
\]

This proves

\[
{\operatorname{Vol}}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {{B}_{{t}_{0}}\left( {p,1}\right) }\right)  \geq  {\kappa }_{0} > 0
\]

for some universal positive constant \( {\kappa }_{0} \) . So we have proved that the ancient \( \kappa \) -solution is also an ancient \( {\kappa }_{0} \) -solution. \( \square \)

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
First, the only nonflat oriented nonnegatively curved gradient shrinking 2-D soliton is the round \( {S}^{2} \) . The reference [30] given in I.11.3 for this fact does not actually cover it, as the reference only deals with compact solitons. A proof using Proposition 39.1 to rule out the noncompact case appears in [68].

Given this, the limit solution in Proposition 39.1 is a shrinking round 2-sphere. Thus the rescalings \( {\bar{\tau }}_{i}^{-1}g\left( {{t}_{0} - {\bar{\tau }}_{i}}\right) \) converge to a round 2-sphere as \( i \rightarrow  \infty \) . However, by [30] the Ricci flow makes an almost-round 2-sphere become more round. Thus any given time slice of the original \( \kappa \) -solution must be a round 2-sphere.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any \( {t}_{0} \geq  0 \) for which there is a standard solution \( g\left( t\right) \) defined on \( \left\lbrack  {0,{T}_{1}}\right\rbrack \) with \( {t}_{0} < {T}_{1} \) , there is \( T > {t}_{0} \) and a solution to Equation (12.19) with initial condition \( \widetilde{\rho }\left( {r,{t}_{0}}\right)  = 0 \) defined on the time-interval \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{0}, T}\right\rbrack \) .

At this point to simplify the notation we shift time by \( - {t}_{0} \) so that our initial time is 0, though our initial metric is not \( {g}_{0} \) but rather is the \( {t}_{0} \) time-slice of the standard solution we are considering, so that now \( {t}_{0} = 0 \) and our initial condition is \( \widetilde{\rho }\left( {r,0}\right)  = 0 \) .

Let \( x = \left( {{x}^{1},\ldots ,{x}^{n + 2}}\right) \) and \( y = \left( {{y}^{1},\ldots ,{y}^{n + 2}}\right) \) be two points in \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n + 1} \) and

\[
H\left( {x, y, t}\right)  = \frac{1}{{\left( 4\pi t\right) }^{\left( {n + 2}\right) /2}}{e}^{-\frac{{\left| x - y\right| }^{2}}{4t}}
\]

be the heat kernel. We solve (12.19) by successive approximation [47].

Define

\[
F\left( {x,\widetilde{\rho },\nabla \widetilde{\rho }, t}\right)  = \nabla \left\lbrack  {\left( {n - 1}\right) \widetilde{h} - B}\right\rbrack   \cdot  \nabla \widetilde{\rho } + {\left| \nabla \widetilde{\rho }\right| }^{2} + G\left( {\widetilde{\rho }, x, t}\right) .
\]

Let \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{0}\left( {x, t}\right)  = 0 \) and for \( i \geq  1 \) we define \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} \) by

(12.20)

\[
{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} = {\int }_{0}^{t}{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}}H\left( {x, y, t - s}\right) F\left( {y,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1},\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}, t}\right) {dyds}
\]

which solves

(12.21)

\[
\frac{\partial {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}}{\partial t} = \bigtriangleup {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} + F\left( {x,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1},\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}, t}\right) \;{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}\left( {x,0}\right)  = 0.
\]

To show the existence of \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} \) by induction, it suffices to prove the following statement: For any \( i \geq  1 \) , if \( \left| {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}\right| ,\left| {\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}}\right| \) are bounded, then \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} \) exists and \( \left| {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}\right| ,\left| {\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}}\right| \) are bounded. Assume \( \left| {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}\right|  \leq  {C}_{1},\left| {\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}}\right|  \leq  {C}_{2} \) are bounded on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) ; then it follows from Claim 12.23 that \( G\left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1},\mathbf{x}, t}\right) \) is bounded on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) ,

\[
\left| {G\left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}, x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{ * }\left( {{C}_{1},\widetilde{h}}\right) ,
\]

and also because of Claim 12.23 both \( \left| {\nabla B}\right| \) and \( \left| {\nabla \widetilde{h}}\right| \) are bounded on all of \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , it follows that \( F\left( {x,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1},\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}, t}\right) \) is bounded:

\[
\left| {F\left( {x,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1},\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \left\lbrack  {\left( {n - 1}\right) \sup \left| {\nabla \widetilde{h}}\right|  + \sup \left| {\nabla B}\right| }\right\rbrack  {C}_{2} + {C}_{2}^{2} + {C}_{ * }\left( {{C}_{1},\widetilde{h}}\right) .
\]

Clearly, the last expression is bounded by a constant \( {C}_{3} \) depending only on the previous bounds. Hence \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} \) exists.

The bounds on \( \left| {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}\right| \) and \( \left| {\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}}\right| \) follow from the estimates

\[
\left| {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}\right|  \leq  {\int }_{0}^{t}{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}}H\left( {x, y, t - s}\right) {C}_{3}{dyds} \leq  {C}_{3}t,
\]

and

\[
\left| {\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}}\right|  = \left| {{\int }_{0}^{t}{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}}\left\lbrack  {{\nabla }_{x}H\left( {x, y, t - s}\right) }\right\rbrack  F\left( {y,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1},\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}, t}\right) {dyds}}\right|
\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{0}^{t}{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}}\left| {{\nabla }_{x}H\left( {x, y, t - s}\right) }\right| {C}_{3}{dyds}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{t}{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}}\frac{1}{{\left( 4\pi \left( t - s\right) \right) }^{\left( {n + 2}\right) /2}}{e}^{-\frac{{\left| x - y\right| }^{2}}{4\left( {t - s}\right) }}\frac{\left| x - y\right| }{2\left( {t - s}\right) }{C}_{3}{dyds}
\]

\[
\leq  \frac{\left( {n + 2}\right) {C}_{3}}{\sqrt{\pi }}{\int }_{0}^{t}\frac{1}{\sqrt{t - s}}{ds} = \frac{2\left( {n + 2}\right) {C}_{3}}{\sqrt{\pi }}\sqrt{t}
\]

Assuming, as we shall, that \( T \leq  \min \left\{  {\frac{{C}_{3}}{{C}_{1}},\frac{\pi {C}_{2}^{2}}{4{\left( n + 2\right) }^{2}{C}_{3}^{2}}}\right\} \) , then for \( 0 \leq  t \leq  T \) we have for all \( i \) ,

(12.22)

\[
\left| {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}\right|  \leq  {C}_{1}\;\text{ and }\;\left| {\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}}\right|  \leq  {C}_{2}.
\]

We prove the convergence of \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} \) to a solution of (12.19) via proving that it is a Cauchy sequence in \( {C}^{1} \) -norm. Note that \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} - {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1} \) satisfies

(12.23)

\[
\frac{\partial \left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} - {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}}\right) }{\partial t} = \bigtriangleup \left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} - {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}}\right)
\]

\[
+ F\left( {x,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1},\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}, t}\right)  - F\left( {x,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 2},\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 2}, t}\right)
\]

with

\[
\left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} - {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}}\right) \left( {x,0}\right)  = 0,
\]

where

\[
F\left( {x,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1},\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}, t}\right)  - F\left( {x,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 2},\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 2}, t}\right)
\]

\[
= \left\lbrack  {\left( {n - 1}\right) \nabla \widetilde{h} - \nabla B + \nabla \left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1} + {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 2}}\right) }\right\rbrack   \cdot  \nabla \left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1} - {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 2}}\right)
\]

\[
+ G\left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1},\mathbf{x}, t}\right)  - G\left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 2},\mathbf{x}, t}\right) .
\]

By lengthy but straightforward calculations one can verify the Lipschitz property of \( G\left( {\widetilde{\rho },\mathbf{x}, t}\right) \) ,

\[
\left| {G\left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1},\mathbf{x}, t}\right)  - G\left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 2},\mathbf{x}, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{\& }\left( {{C}_{1},{C}_{2},\widetilde{f},{\widetilde{f}}_{0}}\right)  \cdot  \left| {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1} - {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 2}}\right| .
\]

This and (12.22) implies

(12.24)

\[
\left| {F\left( {x,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1},\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}, t}\right)  - F\left( {x,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 2},\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 2}, t}\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  {C}_{4} \cdot  \left| {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1} - {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 2}}\right|  + {C}_{5} \cdot  \left| {\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1} - \nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 2}}\right|
\]

where \( {C}_{4} = {C}_{\& }\left( {{C}_{1},{C}_{2},\widetilde{f},{\widetilde{f}}_{0}}\right) \) and \( {C}_{5} = \left\lbrack  {\left( {n - 1}\right) \sup \left| {\nabla \widetilde{f}}\right|  + \sup \left| {\nabla B}\right|  + 2{C}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) .

Let

\[
{A}_{i}\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{0 \leq  s \leq  t, x \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}}}\left| {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} - {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}}\right| \left( {x, s}\right) ,
\]

\[
{B}_{i}\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{0 \leq  s \leq  t, x \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}}}\left| {\nabla \left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} - {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}}\right) }\right| \left( {x, s}\right) .
\]

From Equations (12.23) and (12.24) we can estimate \( \left| {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} - {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}}\right| \) and \( \left| {\nabla \left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} - {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}}\right) }\right| \) in the same way as we estimate \( \left| {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}\right| \) and \( \left| {\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}}\right| \) above; we conclude

\[
{A}_{i}\left( t\right)  \leq  \left\lbrack  {{C}_{4}{A}_{i - 1}\left( t\right)  + {C}_{5}{B}_{i - 1}\left( t\right) }\right\rbrack   \cdot  t
\]

\[
{B}_{i}\left( t\right)  \leq  \frac{2\left( {n + 2}\right) \left\lbrack  {{C}_{4}{A}_{i - 1}\left( t\right)  + {C}_{5}{B}_{i - 1}\left( t\right) }\right\rbrack  }{\sqrt{\pi }} \cdot  \sqrt{t}.
\]

Let \( {C}_{6} = \max \left\{  {{C}_{4},{C}_{5}}\right\} \) ; then we get

\[
{A}_{i}\left( t\right)  + {B}_{i}\left( t\right)  \leq  \left( {{C}_{6}t + \frac{2\left( {n + 2}\right) {C}_{6}\sqrt{t}}{\sqrt{\pi }}}\right)  \cdot  \left( {{A}_{i - 1}\left( t\right)  + {B}_{i - 1}\left( t\right) }\right) .
\]

Now suppose that \( T \leq  {T}_{2} \) where \( {T}_{2} \) satisfies \( {C}_{6}{T}_{2} + \frac{2\left( {n + 2}\right) {C}_{6}\sqrt{{T}_{2}}}{\sqrt{\pi }} = \frac{1}{2} \) ; then for all \( t \leq  T \) we have

\[
{A}_{i}\left( t\right)  + {B}_{i}\left( t\right)  \leq  \frac{1}{2}\left( {{A}_{i - 1}\left( t\right)  + {B}_{i - 1}\left( t\right) }\right) .
\]

This proves that \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} \) is a Cauchy sequence in \( {C}^{1}\left( {\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}\right) \) . Let \( \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow   + \infty }}{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} = {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty } \) . Then \( \nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} \rightarrow  \nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty } \) and \( F\left( {x,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1},\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}, t}\right)  \rightarrow  F\left( {x,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty },\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty }, t}\right) \) uniformly. Hence we get from (12.20),

(12.25)

\[
{\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty } = {\int }_{0}^{t}{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}}H\left( {x, y, t - s}\right) F\left( {y,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty },\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty }, t}\right) {dyds}.
\]

The next argument is similar to the argument in [47], p.21. The function \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} \) is a smooth solution of (12.21) with \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}\left( {x,0}\right)  = 0 \) . Also, both \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i} \) and \( F\left( {x,{\widetilde{\rho }}_{{i}_{1}},\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i - 1}, t}\right) \) are uniformly bounded on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Thus, by Theorems 1.11 on p. 211 and 12.1 on p. 223 of [46], for any compact \( K \subset  {\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2} \) and any \( 0 < {t}_{ * } < T \) , there is \( {C}_{7} \) and \( \alpha  \in  \left( {0,1}\right) \) independent of \( i \) such that

\[
\left| {\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}\left( {x, t}\right)  - \nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}\left( {y, s}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{7} \cdot  \left( {{\left| x - y\right| }^{\alpha } + {\left| t - s\right| }^{\alpha /2}}\right)
\]

where \( x, y \in  K \) and \( 0 \leq  t < s \leq  {t}_{ * } \) .

Letting \( i \rightarrow  \infty \) we get

(12.26)

\[
\left| {\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty }\left( {x, t}\right)  - \nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty }\left( {y, s}\right) }\right|  \leq  {C}_{7} \cdot  \left( {{\left| x - y\right| }^{\alpha } + {\left| t - s\right| }^{\alpha /2}}\right) .
\]

Hence \( \nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty } \in  {C}^{\alpha ,\alpha /2} \) . That is to say \( \nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty } \) is \( \alpha \) -Hölder continuous in space and \( \alpha /2 \) -Hölder continuous in time. From (12.25) we conclude that \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty } \) is a solution of (12.19) on \( {\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) with \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty }\left( {x,0}\right)  = 0 \) .

7.5. The asymptotic behavior of the solutions. In the rest of this subsection we study the asymptotic behavior of solution \( \widetilde{\rho }\left( {x, t}\right) \) as \( x \rightarrow  \infty \) . First we prove inductively that there is a constant \( \lambda \) and \( {T}_{3} \) such that, provided that \( T \leq  {T}_{3} \) , for \( x \in  {\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}, t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , we have

(12.27)

\[
\left| {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{\lambda }{{\left( 1 + \left| x\right| \right) }^{2}}\;\text{ and }\;\left| {\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{\lambda }{{\left( 1 + \left| x\right| \right) }^{2}}.
\]

Clearly, since \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{0} = 0 \) , these estimates hold for \( i = 0 \) . It follows from (12.22) and Claim 12.23 that there is a constant \( {C}_{8} \) independent of \( i \) such that

\[
\left| {G\left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i},\mathbf{x}, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{{C}_{8}}{{\left( 1 + \left| x\right| \right) }^{2}}
\]

\[
\left\lbrack  {\left( {n - 1}\right) \left| {\nabla \widetilde{h}}\right|  + \left| {\nabla B}\right| }\right\rbrack  \left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  {C}_{8}.
\]

Now we assume these estimates hold for \( i \) . Then for \( 0 \leq  t \leq  T \) we have

\[
\left| {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|
\]

\[
\leq  {\int }_{0}^{t}{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}}H\left( {x, y, t - s}\right) \left\lbrack  {\frac{{C}_{8}\lambda }{{\left( 1 + \left| y\right| \right) }^{2}} + \frac{{\lambda }^{2}}{{\left( 1 + \left| y\right| \right) }^{2}} + \frac{{C}_{8}}{{\left( 1 + \left| y\right| \right) }^{2}}}\right\rbrack  {dyds}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{t}{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}}\frac{1}{{\left( 4\pi \left( t - s\right) \right) }^{\left( {n + 2}\right) /2}}{e}^{-\frac{{\left| x - y\right| }^{2}}{4\left( {t - s}\right) }}\left\lbrack  \frac{{C}_{8}\lambda  + {\lambda }^{2} + {C}_{8}}{{\left( 1 + \left| y\right| \right) }^{2}}\right\rbrack  {dyds}
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {{C}_{8}\lambda  + {\lambda }^{2} + {C}_{8}}\right)  \cdot  \frac{C\left( n\right) t}{{\left( 1 + \left| x\right| \right) }^{2}}.
\]

Also, we have

\[
\left| {\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{i}\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  {\int }_{0}^{t}{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}}\left| {{\nabla }_{x}H\left( {x, y, t - s}\right) }\right| \left\lbrack  \frac{{C}_{8}\lambda  + {\lambda }^{2} + {C}_{8}}{{\left( 1 + \left| y\right| \right) }^{2}}\right\rbrack  {dyds}
\]

\[
= {\int }_{0}^{t}{\int }_{{\mathbb{R}}^{n + 2}}\frac{\left| x - y\right| }{2\left( {t - s}\right) }\frac{1}{{\left( 4\pi \left( t - s\right) \right) }^{\left( {n + 2}\right) /2}}{e}^{-\frac{{\left| x - y\right| }^{2}}{4\left( {t - s}\right) }}\left\lbrack  \frac{{C}_{8}\lambda  + {\lambda }^{2} + {C}_{8}}{{\left( 1 + \left| y\right| \right) }^{2}}\right\rbrack  {dyds}
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {{C}_{8}\lambda  + {\lambda }^{2} + {C}_{8}}\right)  \cdot  \frac{C\left( n\right) \sqrt{t}}{{\left( 1 + \left| x\right| \right) }^{2}}.
\]

If we choose \( {T}_{3} \) such that

\[
\left( {{C}_{8}\lambda  + {\lambda }^{2} + {C}_{8}}\right)  \cdot  C\left( n\right) {T}_{3} \leq  \lambda \;\text{ and }\;\left( {{C}_{8}\lambda  + {\lambda }^{2} + {C}_{8}}\right)  \cdot  C\left( n\right) \sqrt{{T}_{3}} \leq  \lambda ,
\]

then (12.27) hold for all \( i \) . From the definition of \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty } \) we conclude that

(12.28)

\[
\left| {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty }\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{\lambda }{{\left( 1 + \left| x\right| \right) }^{2}}\text{ and }\left| {\nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty }\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \frac{\lambda }{{\left( 1 + \left| x\right| \right) }^{2}}.
\]

Recall that \( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty } \) is a solution of the following linear equation (in \( v \) ):

\[
\frac{\partial v}{\partial t} = {\Delta v} + \nabla \left\lbrack  {\left( {n - 1}\right) \widetilde{h} - B}\right\rbrack   \cdot  \nabla v + G\left( {{\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty },\mathbf{x}, t}\right) ,
\]

\[
v\left( {x,0}\right)  = 0.
\]

From (12.26) and Claim 12.23 we know that \( \nabla \left\lbrack  {\left( {n - 1}\right) \widetilde{h} - B + {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty }}\right\rbrack \) has \( {C}^{\alpha ,\alpha /2} \) -Hölder-norm bounded (this means \( \alpha \) -Hölder norm in space and the \( \alpha /2 \) -Hölder norm in time). By some lengthy calculations we get

\[
{\left| G\left( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty },\mathbf{x}, t\right) \right| }_{{C}^{\alpha ,\alpha /2}} \leq  \frac{{C}_{9}}{{\left( 1 + \left| x\right| \right) }^{2}}.
\]

By local Schauder estimates for parabolic equations we conclude

\[
{\left| {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty }\right| }_{{C}^{2 + \alpha ,1 + \alpha /2}} \leq  \frac{{C}_{10}}{{\left( 1 + \left| x\right| \right) }^{2}}.
\]

Using this estimate one can further show by calculation that

\[
{\left. \left| \nabla \nabla \left\lbrack  \left( n - 1\right) \widetilde{f} - B + {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty }\right\rbrack  \right| \right| }_{{C}^{\alpha ,\alpha /2}} \leq  {C}_{11}
\]

\[
{\left| \nabla G\left( {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty },\mathbf{x}, t\right) \right| }_{{C}^{\alpha ,\alpha /2}} \leq  \frac{{C}_{12}}{{\left( 1 + \left| x\right| \right) }^{2}}.
\]

By local high order Schauder estimates for parabolic equations we conclude

\[
{\left| \nabla {\widetilde{\rho }}_{\infty }\right| }_{{C}^{2 + \alpha ,1 + \alpha /2}} \leq  \frac{{C}_{13}}{{\left( 1 + \left| x\right| \right) }^{2}}.
\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose that \( g\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , is a complete solution to the Ricci flow on a noncompact manifold \( {\mathcal{M}}^{n} \) with \( \left| {\operatorname{Rm}\left( {g\left( t\right) }\right) }\right|  \leq  {k}_{0} \) for some \( {k}_{0} > 0 \) . Let \( L \) be defined by (10.1), i.e.,

\[
{Lu} \Doteq  \frac{\partial u}{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }u - \langle X\left( t\right) ,\nabla u\rangle  - F\left( {u, t}\right) ,
\]

where \( X\left( t\right) \) is a smooth family of bounded vector fields and the function \( F : \mathbb{R} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \mathbb{R} \) is locally Lipschitz in the \( \mathbb{R} \) factor and continuous in the \( \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) factor. Suppose that \( u \in  {C}^{2,1} \) satisfies

(12.16)

\[
{Lu} \leq  0\;\text{ and }\;\left| {u\left( {x, t}\right) }\right|  \leq  \exp \left( {\widetilde{b}\left( {{d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right) }\right)
\]

for some constant \( \widetilde{b} \) . For any constant \( c \in  \mathbb{R} \) , let \( U\left( t\right) \) be the solution to the corresponding ordinary differential equation:

(12.17)

\[
\frac{dU}{dt} = F\left( {U, t}\right) ,
\]

(12.18)

\[
U\left( 0\right)  = c.
\]

If \( u\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  c \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) , then we have

(12.19)

\[
u\left( {x, t}\right)  \leq  U\left( t\right)
\]

for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) as long as the solution to the ODE exists.

knowledge_statements.proof_latex:
Proof. Consider the difference between the subsolution to the PDE and the solution to the ODE:

\[
v \Doteq  u - U
\]

By \( {Lu} \leq  0,\left( {12.17}\right) \) , and our initial assumptions on \( u \) and \( U \) , we have

(12.20)

\[
{L}_{0}v \Doteq  \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) } - {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }}\right) v \leq  F\left( {u, t}\right)  - F\left( {U, t}\right)
\]

and \( v\left( {x,0}\right)  \leq  0 \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Let

\[
\widetilde{u} \Doteq  {e}^{-{A}_{1}t}v
\]

where the constant \( {A}_{1} \) is to be chosen sufficiently large below. Let \( \phi \) be the barrier supersolution given by Lemma 12.9, where \( A = 0 \) in (12.10), where \( a = 2\widetilde{b} \) in (12.11), and where \( \widetilde{b} \) is as in (12.16).

Claim. For any \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) we have

\[
\widetilde{u} \leq  {\varepsilon \phi }\;\text{ on }\mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack
\]

By taking \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) , we then have \( \widetilde{u} \leq  0 \) on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) and the lemma follows directly. \( {}^{9} \)

Now we prove the claim by contradiction. If the claim is false, then there exists \( \left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right) \) such that

\[
\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {{x}_{1},{t}_{1}}\right)  > 0.
\]

On the other hand, by the assumption (12.16) on the growth of \( u \) and the lower bound (12.9) for \( \phi \) we have \( \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {x, t}\right)  < 0 \) for \( {d}_{g\left( 0\right) }\left( {O, x}\right) \) sufficiently large independent of \( t \) ; in fact \( \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {x, t}\right)  \rightarrow   - \infty \) as \( {d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  \rightarrow \; \infty \) uniformly in \( t \) . Note also that \( \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {x,0}\right)  < 0 \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) . Hence there exists \( {t}_{0} \in  \left( {0,{t}_{1}}\right) \) and \( {x}_{0} \in  \mathcal{M} \) such that

\[
\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {x, t}\right)  < 0\;\text{ for all }\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0,{t}_{0}}\right)
\]

---

\( {}^{9} \) Note that considering \( \widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi } \) is analogous to considering \( v \) in (12.3).

---

and

(12.21)

\[
\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right) \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  = 0.
\]

By the locally Lipschitz property of \( F \) there exists a constant \( {K}_{0} \) independent of \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) with (12.21) and \( {A}_{1} \geq  0 \) (but depending on \( \varepsilon \) ) such that \( {}^{10} \)

\[
\left| {F\left( {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\right)  - F\left( {U\left( {t}_{0}\right) ,{t}_{0}}\right) }\right|  \leq  {K}_{0}\left| {u\left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right)  - U\left( {t}_{0}\right) }\right| .
\]

Therefore (12.20) implies at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) ,{}^{11} \)

\[
{L}_{0}\widetilde{u} = \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) } - {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }}\right) \widetilde{u}
\]

\[
\leq  {e}^{-{A}_{1}t}\left( {F\left( {u, t}\right)  - F\left( {U, t}\right) }\right)  - {A}_{1}\widetilde{u}
\]

\[
\leq  \left( {{K}_{0} - {A}_{1}}\right) \widetilde{u}.
\]

By the first and second derivative tests, at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) we have

\[
\frac{\partial }{\partial t}\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right)  \geq  0
\]

and

\[
{\nabla }_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right)  = 0,\;{\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Hence, using (12.10), at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) we have

\[
0 \leq  \left( {\frac{\partial }{\partial t} - {\Delta }_{g\left( t\right) } - {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }}\right) \left( {\widetilde{u} - {\varepsilon \phi }}\right)
\]

\[
= {L}_{0}\widetilde{u} - \varepsilon {L}_{0}\phi  \leq  \left( {{K}_{0} - {A}_{1}}\right) \widetilde{u}
\]

\[
= \left( {{K}_{0} - {A}_{1}}\right) {\varepsilon \phi }
\]

since \( {L}_{0}\phi  \geq  0 \) . Choosing \( {A}_{1} > {K}_{0} \) , we obtain a contradiction and the theorem is proved.

(Maximum principle for systems: time-dependent sets). Let \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right)  \subset  \mathcal{V} \) be subsets which are invariant under parallel translation by \( \nabla \left( t\right) \) for each \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . We require that \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \doteq  \mathcal{K}\left( t\right)  \cap  {\mathcal{V}}_{x} \) be closed and convex and that the space-time track

\[
\mathcal{T} \Doteq  \{ \left( {v, t}\right)  \in  \mathcal{V} \times  \mathbb{R} : v \in  \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) ,0 \leq  t \leq  T\}
\]

---

\( {}^{23} \) Note that for any \( \widetilde{V} \) with \( \left| \widetilde{V}\right|  = 1 \) at \( \left( {{x}_{0},{t}_{0}}\right) \) , we have \( \left| {\left( {u + {\varepsilon \phi }\widetilde{h}}\right) \left( {\widetilde{V},\widetilde{V}}\right) }\right|  \leq \; 2{e}^{\widehat{a}\left( {{C}_{1} + 1}\right) } \) .

---

also be closed in \( \mathcal{V} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) . Assume that \( F\left( {u, t}\right) \) is continuous in \( \left( {u, t}\right) \) and locally Lipschitz in u. Suppose that, for any \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and initial time \( {t}_{0} \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , any solution \( U\left( t\right) \) of the ODE (10.63) which starts in \( \mathcal{K}{\left( {t}_{0}\right) }_{x} \) will remain in \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) for all later times as long as the solution exists. Let \( u\left( t\right) \) , \( t \in  \lbrack 0, T) \) , be a solution of the PDE (10.24) which satisfies

\[
d\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x}}\right)  \leq  \exp \left( {\widehat{a}\left( {{d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {O, x}\right)  + 1}\right) }\right)
\]

on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) for some \( \widehat{a} \) and \( O \in  \mathcal{M} \) . If \( u \) starts in \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) at \( t = 0 \) (i.e., \( u\left( {x,0}\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( 0\right) }_{x} \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) ), then \( u \) stays in \( \mathcal{K}\left( t\right) \) for all \( t \in  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) (i.e., \( u\left( {x, t}\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x} \) for all \( x \) and \( t \) ).

For any \( v \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{x} \) , define

\[
{\rho }_{t}\left( v\right)  \Doteq  d\left( {v,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x}}\right) .
\]

Fixing \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) , the function \( {\rho }_{t}\left( \cdot \right) \) is Lipschitz on \( {\mathcal{V}}_{x} \) . Consider the function

\[
{\rho }_{t}\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {x, t}\right)
\]

on \( \mathcal{M} \times  \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) , where \( \phi \) is given in Lemma 12.9 so that (12.10) and (12.11) hold for \( a \Doteq  \widehat{a} + 1 \) and \( A \) to be chosen later. Taking the spatial supremum of the above function, we define \( s : \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack   \rightarrow  \lbrack 0,\infty ) \) by

\[
s\left( t\right)  \Doteq  \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  \mathcal{M}}}\left( {d\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) .
\]

Claim. For all \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) we have \( s\left( t\right)  \leq  0 \) for all \( t \geq  0 \) .

Assuming the claim and taking the limit as \( \varepsilon  \rightarrow  0 \) , we obtain the proposition.

We now prove the claim. Suppose the claim is false; then there exists a solution \( u\left( {x, t}\right) \) of the PDE (10.24) on \( \left\lbrack  {0, T}\right\rbrack \) such that \( u\left( {x,0}\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}\left( 0\right) \) for all \( x \in  \mathcal{M} \) and \( s\left( {t}_{2}\right)  > 0 \) for some \( {t}_{2} \in  \left( {0, T}\right) \) . Since the space-time track \( \mathcal{T} \) is closed, by a proof similar to that of Lemma 10.65, \( s \) is lower semicontinuous and right continuous at any \( t \) with \( s\left( t\right)  > 0 \) . Hence there exists a time \( {t}_{1} \geq  0 \) such that \( s\left( {t}_{1}\right)  = 0, s\left( t\right)  > 0 \) for any \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) , and \( s\left( t\right) \) is lower semi-continuous and right continuous on \( \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . By Corollary 10.26 the claim follows from showing \( \frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt} \leq  {Cs} \) on \( \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) .

Now we turn to proving \( \frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt} \leq  {Cs} \) on \( \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) . For \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack \) , since \( d\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{x}}\right)  > 0 \) for some \( x \in  \mathcal{M}, s\left( t\right) \) may be written as

\[
s\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{x \in  \mathcal{M}}}\left\{  {\left( {\mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {v,\ell }\right)  \in  {\mathcal{S}}_{x}\left( t\right) }}\ell \left( {u\left( {x, t}\right)  - v}\right) }\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {x, t}\right) }\right\}
\]

\[
= \mathop{\sup }\limits_{{\left( {v,\ell , x}\right)  \in  \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) }}\left( {g\left( {v,\ell , x, t}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {x, t}\right) }\right) ,
\]

where \( \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) \) is defined as in (10.66), and as in Chapter 10,

\[
g\left( {v,\ell , x, t}\right)  \Doteq  \ell \left( {u\left( {x, t}\right)  - v}\right) ,\;\text{ for }\left( {v,\ell , x}\right)  \in  \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) , t \in  \left\lbrack  {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right\rbrack  .
\]

Given \( t \in  \left( {{t}_{1},{t}_{2}}\right) \) , let \( {h}_{i} \searrow  0 \) be such that

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{s\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - s\left( t\right) }{{h}_{i}}.
\]

From the growth assumption on \( u \) and (12.11), it is easy to see that

\[
{\rho }_{t}\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right) }\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {x, t}\right)  < 0
\]

when \( {d}_{g\left( t\right) }\left( {x, O}\right)  \geq  {C}_{1} \) , where \( {C}_{1} \) is sufficiently large independent of \( t \) . Hence there exist sequences \( {x}_{i} \in  \mathcal{M},{v}_{i} \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t + {h}_{i}\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) , and \( {\ell }_{i} \in  {S}_{{v}_{i}}\mathcal{K}{\left( t + {h}_{i}\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) such that

\[
g\left( {{v}_{i},{\ell }_{i},{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  = s\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right) .
\]

For the same reason as above, there exists a subsequence such that \( {x}_{i} \rightarrow \; {x}_{\infty } \in  \mathcal{M},{v}_{i} \rightarrow  {v}_{\infty } \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) , and \( {\ell }_{i} \rightarrow  {\ell }_{\infty } \in  {S}_{{v}_{\infty }}\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \subset  {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{\infty }}^{ * } \) . Since \( g \) is continuous and \( s \) is right continuous, we have

(12.43)

\[
s\left( t\right)  = g\left( {{v}_{\infty },{\ell }_{\infty },{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  = {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) .
\]

We compute(12.44)

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{g\left( {{v}_{i},{\ell }_{i},{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - g\left( {{v}_{\infty },{\ell }_{\infty },{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  + {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }{{h}_{i}}
\]

\[
- \varepsilon \frac{\partial \phi }{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)
\]

\[
= \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{\ell }_{i}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - {v}_{i}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  + {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }{{h}_{i}}
\]

\[
- \varepsilon \frac{\partial \phi }{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) .
\]

Choose \( {v}_{i}^{ * } \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) and \( {\ell }_{i}^{ * } \in  {S}_{{v}_{i}^{ * }}\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) such that

(12.45)

\[
d\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{i}}}\right)  = {\ell }_{i}^{ * }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }}\right)  = {\left| u\left( {x}_{i}, t\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }\right| }_{h}.
\]

Let \( {U}_{i}\left( \tau \right) ,\tau  \in  \lbrack t, t + \varepsilon ) \) , for some \( \varepsilon  > 0 \) independent of \( i \) , be the solution to the ODE (10.63) in \( {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{i}} \) :

(12.46)

\[
\frac{d{U}_{i}}{d\tau } = F\left( {{U}_{i},\tau }\right)
\]

with \( {U}_{i}\left( t\right)  = {v}_{i}^{ * } \) . Define \( {F}_{i} \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{i}} \) by

(12.47)

\[
{v}_{i}^{ * } + {h}_{i}{F}_{i} = {U}_{i}\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right) .
\]

By our assumption, we have \( {U}_{i}\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( t + {h}_{i}\right) }_{{x}_{i}} \) . Hence

(12.48)

\[
{\ell }_{i}\left( {{v}_{i}^{ * } + {h}_{i}{F}_{i} - {v}_{i}}\right)  \leq  0.
\]

Note that (12.46) and (12.47) imply that as \( i \rightarrow  \infty \) ,

\[
\left| {{F}_{i} - F\left( {{v}_{i}^{ * }, t}\right) }\right|  = \left| {\frac{{U}_{i}\left( {t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - {U}_{i}\left( t\right) }{{h}_{i}} - \frac{d{U}_{i}}{dt}\left( t\right) }\right|  \rightarrow  0.
\]

By passing to a subsequence, we have \( {v}_{i}^{ * } \rightarrow  {v}_{\infty }^{ * } \in  \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) and \( {\ell }_{i}^{ * } \rightarrow  {\ell }_{\infty }^{ * } \) . We claim that \( {v}_{\infty }^{ * } = {v}_{\infty } \) . Taking the limit of (12.45), we have

\[
\left| {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }^{ * }}\right|  = {\ell }_{\infty }^{ * }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }^{ * }}\right)
\]

\[
= d\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }}}\right)
\]

\[
= \left| {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right| ,
\]

where the last equality follows from (12.43). Since \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) is convex, we conclude that \( {v}_{\infty }^{ * } = {v}_{\infty } \) . (The point \( {v}_{\infty } \in  \partial \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) is the unique point in \( \mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }} \) closest to \( u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) \) .)

From (10.68) we have

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)  = \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\left\lbrack  {{\ell }_{i}\left( {\frac{u\left( {{x}_{i}, t + {h}_{i}}\right)  - u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right) }{{h}_{i}} - {F}_{i}}\right)  + \frac{{\ell }_{i}\left( {{v}_{i}^{ * } + {h}_{i}{F}_{i} - {v}_{i}}\right) }{{h}_{i}}}\right\rbrack
\]

\[
+ \mathop{\lim }\limits_{{i \rightarrow  \infty }}\frac{{\ell }_{i}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  + {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }{{h}_{i}}
\]

\[
- \varepsilon \frac{\partial \phi }{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) .
\]

Note that for each \( i \) ,

\[
{\ell }_{i}\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  \left| {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)  - {v}_{i}^{ * }}\right|  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)
\]

\[
= d\left( {u\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{i}}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{i}, t}\right)
\]

\[
\leq  d\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) ,\mathcal{K}{\left( t\right) }_{{x}_{\infty }}}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)
\]

\[
= {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) .
\]

From (12.43) we also have that \( \left( {{v}_{\infty },{\ell }_{\infty },{x}_{\infty }}\right)  \in  \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) \) satisfies

\[
{\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  = s\left( t\right) ,
\]

so that by parallel translating \( {v}_{\infty } \) and \( {\ell }_{\infty } \) along geodesics (with respect to \( g\left( t\right) ) \) emanating from \( {x}_{\infty } \) , so that \( \left( {{v}_{\infty }\left( x\right) ,{\ell }_{\infty }\left( x\right) , x}\right)  \in  \mathcal{R}\left( t\right) \) for \( x \) in a neighborhood of \( {x}_{\infty } \) , we have

\[
\nabla \left( {{\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }\right)  = 0
\]

\[
\Delta \left\lbrack  {{\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u - {v}_{\infty }}\right)  - {\varepsilon \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }\right\rbrack  \left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  = {\ell }_{\infty }\left\lbrack  {{\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) }\right\rbrack   - {\varepsilon \Delta \phi } \leq  0
\]

since \( {\ell }_{\infty } \) is linear (note that \( {\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  \in  {\mathcal{V}}_{{x}_{\infty }} \) and that \( {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {u\left( {x, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right) \) is a real-valued function in a neighborhood of \( {x}_{\infty } \) which achieves a local maximum at \( {x}_{\infty } \) ). From this, (12.48), (12.10), and 12.11, we have

\[
\frac{{d}^{ + }s}{dt}\left( t\right)  \leq  {\ell }_{\infty }\left( {\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - F\left( {{v}_{\infty }^{ * }, t}\right) }\right)  - \varepsilon \frac{\partial \phi }{\partial t}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)
\]

\[
= {\ell }_{\infty }\left\lbrack  {{\Delta u}\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  + {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  + F\left( {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right) , t}\right)  - F\left( {{v}_{\infty }^{ * }, t}\right) }\right\rbrack
\]

\[
- {\varepsilon \Delta \phi }\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {\varepsilon A\phi }
\]

\[
\leq  C\left| {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right|  + \varepsilon {\nabla }_{X\left( t\right) }\phi \left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {\varepsilon A\phi }
\]

\[
\leq  C\left| {u\left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {v}_{\infty }}\right|  + {C}_{2}\phi \left( {{x}_{\infty }, t}\right)  - {\varepsilon A\phi } \leq  {Cs}\left( t\right) ,
\]

where we choose \( A \geq  C + \frac{{C}_{2}}{\varepsilon } \) . This completes the proof of the theorem.
